newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Christian Coalition confident of 10 pct vote.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Christian Coalition confident of 10 pct vote.

text.p: Christian Coalition co-leader the Reverend Graham Capill is confident the coalition can hit 10 percent support on election day, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Tuesday.

Speaking in Palmerston North on Monday, Capill said the party was happy with 5.8 percent in recent polls -- which would give it a "reasonably sized team" -- but was aiming for 10 percent. In some electorates it was already polling eight to nine percent.
The party's support didn't go up and down like other parties, and Capill expected it to continue to rise steadily.

"We've always said that the sort of people voting for us aren't doing it out of a protest vote or an emotional stance, but are actually considering the principles we're putting forward and they agree with them."
He believed some voters wouldn't admit to pollsters they would vote for the coalition, and therefore its election night support might be surprising.

The Christian Coalition was willing to talk to any parties about a coalition. The ruling National party was not its only option, but any party interested in forming a coalition would have to accept the Christian Coalition's non-negotiable policy

One possibility is the party not being in a formal coalition, but agreeing to support a government on matters of supply and confidence, and then voting on each piece of legislation as it came forward.
New Zealand will on October 12 hold its first general election under a new Mixed Member Proportional (MMP) system, which favours a minority or coalition government.
